'''Timothy John Mitchison''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} is a [[cell biologist]] and [[systems biology|systems biologist]] and [[Hasib Sabbagh]] Professor of Systems Biology at [[Harvard Medical School]] in the United States.<ref name="currentbio">{{Cite journal
| last1 = Wells | first1 = William
| title = Tim Mitchison: Dynamic productivity
| journal = Current Biology
| volume = 7
| issue = 11
| pages = R666–R667
| year = 1997
| pmid = 9382812
| doi = 10.1016/S0960-9822(06)00346-0
| doi-access = free
| bibcode = 1997CBio....7R.666W
}}</ref><ref name="harvard">{{cite web|url=https://harvardmagazine.com/2003/11/timothy-mitchison.html|title=Timothy Mitchison|date=November 2003}}</ref><ref name="IshiharaNguyen2014">{{cite journal|last1=Ishihara|first1=K.|last2=Nguyen|first2=P. A.|last3=Wuhr|first3=M.|last4=Groen|first4=A. C.|last5=Field|first5=C. M.|last6=Mitchison|first6=T. J.|title=Organization of early frog embryos by chemical waves emanating from centrosomes|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences|volume=369|issue=1650|year=2014|article-number=20130454|issn=0962-8436|doi=10.1098/rstb.2013.0454|pmid=25047608 |pmc=4113098}}</ref> He is known for his discovery, with [[Marc Kirschner]], of dynamic instability in microtubules,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://bioscience.jbpub.com/cells/EXP93.aspx|title=Great Experiments: Dynamic Instability of Microtubules - Marc Kirschner and Tim Mitchison|last=Lewin|first=Ben|year=2007|access-date=9 February 2019|archive-date=17 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017121343/http://bioscience.jbpub.com/cells/EXP93.aspx}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nature.com/milestones/milecyto/full/milecyto14.html|title=Milestone 14: Nature Milestones in Cytoskeleton|website=Nature|access-date=2019-02-09}}</ref> for studies of the mechanism of cell division, and for contributions to [[chemical biology]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Mitchison|first=T. J.|year=1994|title=Towards a pharmacological genetics|journal=Chemistry & Biology|volume=1|issue=1|pages=3–6|issn=1074-5521|pmid=9383364|doi=10.1016/1074-5521(94)90034-5}}</ref>

== Education and early life ==
Mitchison was educated at [[Haberdashers' Aske's Boys' School]] and completed his Bachelor of Arts degree in [[Biochemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]] where he was an undergraduate student of [[Merton College, Oxford]], from 1976 to 1979. He moved to the [[University of California, San Francisco]] (UCSF) in 1979 for his PhD which was supervised by [[Marc Kirschner]]<ref name=tjmphd>{{cite thesis|first=Timothy John|last=Mitchison|year=1984|degree=PhD|publisher=University of California, San Francisco|title=Structure and Dynamics of Organized Microtubule Arrays|oclc=1020493513|id={{ProQuest|303337748}}}} {{closed access}}</ref> and investigated the dynamic instability of [[microtubule]]s.<ref name=tjmphd/><ref name=MitchisonKirschner1984>{{cite journal|last1=Mitchison|first1=Tim|last2=Kirschner|first2=Marc|title=Dynamic instability of microtubule growth|journal=Nature|pmid=6504138|volume=312|issue=5991|year=1984|pages=237–242|issn=0028-0836|doi=10.1038/312237a0|bibcode=1984Natur.312..237M|s2cid=30079133}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Mitchison returned to the UK for [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[National Institute for Medical Research]] (NIMR) in London.{{when|date=September 2018}} In 1988 he returned to San Francisco where he was appointed assistant professor at UCSF.<ref name="nas" /> In 1994 he wrote an opinion piece for the journal ''Chemistry & Biology'' titled "Towards a pharmacological genetics" which helped to launch the field of [[chemical genetics]].<ref name=":1" /> In 1997 he moved to [[Harvard University]] to become co-director of the Institute for Chemistry and Cell Biology at [[Harvard Medical School]],<ref name="nas" /> where he pioneered phenotype-based screening,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mayer|first1=T. U.|last2=Kapoor|first2=T. M.|last3=Haggarty|first3=S. J.|last4=King|first4=R. W.|last5=Schreiber|first5=S. L.|last6=Mitchison|first6=T. J.|date=1999-10-29|title=Small molecule inhibitor of mitotic spindle bipolarity identified in a phenotype-based screen|journal=Science|volume=286|issue=5441|pages=971–974|issn=0036-8075|pmid=10542155|doi=10.1126/science.286.5441.971|url=https://kops.uni-konstanz.de/bitstream/123456789/14056/2/mayer_140561.pdf}}</ref> discovering the small molecule [[monastrol]] – the first small-molecule inhibitor of [[mitosis]] that does not target [[tubulin]]. [[Monastrol]] was shown to inhibit [[kinesin-5]], a motor protein. In 2003 he became Deputy Chair of the newly formed Department of Systems Biology, chaired by [[Marc Kirschner]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2003/09/hms-launches-new-department-to-study-systems-biology/|title=HMS launches new department to study systems biology|date=2003-09-25|website=Harvard Gazette|access-date=2019-02-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Check|first=Erika|date=2003-10-02|title=Harvard heralds fresh take on systems biology|journal=Nature|volume=425|issue=6957|page=439|doi=10.1038/425439a|pmid=14523408|issn=1476-4687|bibcode=2003Natur.425..439C|doi-access=free}}</ref> He works on aspects of mesoscale biology<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sear|first1=Richard P.|last2=Pagonabarraga|first2=Ignacio|last3=Flaus|first3=Andrew|date=2015-02-25|title=Life at the mesoscale: the self-organised cytoplasm and nucleoplasm|journal=BMC Biophysics|volume=8|issue=1|page=4|doi=10.1186/s13628-015-0018-6|issn=2046-1682|pmc=4374369|pmid=25815164 |doi-access=free }}</ref> including the self-organization of the cytoskeleton<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Mitchison|first=T. J.|date=1992-04-29|title=Self-organization of polymer-motor systems in the cytoskeleton|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series B, Biological Sciences|volume=336|issue=1276|pages=99–106|doi=10.1098/rstb.1992.0049|issn=0962-8436|pmid=1351302|bibcode=1992RSPTB.336...99M}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Ishihara|first1=Keisuke|last2=Nguyen|first2=Phuong A.|last3=Wühr|first3=Martin|last4=Groen|first4=Aaron C.|last5=Field|first5=Christine M.|last6=Mitchison|first6=Timothy J.|date=2014-09-05|title=Organization of early frog embryos by chemical waves emanating from centrosomes|journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. journal|last=Mitchison|first=Timothy J.|date=2010-11-15|title=Remaining mysteries of the cytoplasm|journal=Molecular Biology of the Cell|volume=21|issue=22|pages=3811–3812|doi=10.1091/mbc.E10-02-0084|issn=1939-4586|pmc=2982103|pmid=21079024}}</ref><ref>{{Cite ===Awards and honors===
Mitchison was elected [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 1997 for "substantial contributions to the improvement of natural knowledge"<ref name=frs>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/timothy-mitchison-11966/|website=royalsociety|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=1997|title=Professor Timothy Mitchison FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|"All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]]." --{{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/|title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies|date=2016-11-11}}}}</ref> and served as president of the [[American Society for Cell Biology]] (ASCB) in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ascb.org/ascb-presidents/|title=ASCB Presidents|website=ASCB|access-date=2019-02-09}}</ref> He was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] of the United States in 2014<ref name=nas>{{cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/timothy-j-mitchison-yvuw3n/|title=Timothy Mitchison|website=nasonline.org}}</ref> and delivered the [[Keith R. Porter Lecture]] in 2013.

==Personal life==
Mitchison is married to scientist [[Christine M. Field]] with whom he has two children.<ref name="harvard" /> Mitchison comes from a family of distinguished biologists; his father is [[Avrion Mitchison]],<ref name=currentbio/> his uncles are [[Denis Mitchison]]{{citation needed|date=September 2018}} and [[Murdoch Mitchison]],<ref name=currentbio/> his great uncle was [[J.B.S. Haldane]]<ref name=currentbio/> and his great-grandfather [[John Scott Haldane]].  His grandparents were the politician [[Dick Mitchison]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/obituary-naomi-mitchison-1046691.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/obituary-naomi-mitchison-1046691.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Obituary: Naomi Mitchison|date=1999-01-13|website=The Independent|access-date=2019-02-09}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and the writer [[Naomi Mitchison]] (née Haldane).<ref name=":0" />  His younger sister Hannah M. Mitchison is also a biologist.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Gene mutation identified in PCD, rare disease|journal=Nature Middle East|doi=10.1038/nmiddleeast.2018.62|year = 2018|last1 = Elmeshad|first1 = Sarah|s2cid=90633419 }}</ref>
